what: Out-of-state pass of the route time audit (owner: "yes audit routes outside WA too"). The 52 alpine-family rows outside WA that store a time, a distance or gain, or are on a classics list were researched online in 4 batches; the remaining 5,133 out-of-state rows store none of those.
status: WRITTEN. The project was restarted by the owner after the outage; every repair below was previewed through planTimes, dry-run, written compare-and-set 1000 ms apart with a rollback file (copied to the main checkout's scripts/), and re-run to reconcile (ALREADY).

passes.classicsAndStoredRows: The 52 out-of-state rows that store a time, distance or gain, or are on a classics list: 3 repairs (Bugaboo, Petit Grepon, Mount Hood).
passes.summitLegWithNoApproach: A census of every timed alpine-family row (858, from this session's snapshot) found 30 that store a summit leg but no approach and get the Planner's walk-in added IN FRONT of it (whole-day rows are unaffected). Each was researched for where its stored summit leg starts. Where it already starts at the CAR, the walk was counted twice and the fix is approach 0 (5 repairs); where it starts at a CAMP, the walk-in is the right addition and the row was left.
passes.tradeRoutes: Empty rows on well-climbed peaks (CO 14ers, state highpoints, volcanoes, Tetons, Whitney): 191 matched by AREA name, narrowed to 84 trade routes (scrambles, snow routes, 3rd/4th class). 6 repairs: 3 full sets (Sherman SW Ridge, Capitol Knife-Edge, South Sister South Side) and 3 lone approaches (Sunlight, Windom, Middle Sister SE Ridge).

repairs.why: Empty row. The Alpine Club of Canada's Conrad Kain Hut page gives the walk from the parking lot to the hut, the camp for this route, as 3-4 hr (4.6 km, ~720 m). Stored as a lone approach, which the Planner treats as a floor (#2859); the climb stays unknown.

Empty row (Petit Grepon South Face). Two timed reports from the Glacier Gorge trailhead agree on the walk to the base: 2 hr (2024) and 2 hr 15 (2020), median 2.1. Stored as a lone approach floor (#2859). Car to car in the same reports is 8-8.8 hr, but a lone total is not written.

The row stored 7 hr to the summit and 4 down but no approach, so the Planner added its own 4.8 hr walk-in IN FRONT of a summit leg that already starts at the Timberline lot (15.8 hr car to car beside a stored 12). Every source gives it as a day trip from Timberline Lodge with no separate approach; approach 0 makes the stored legs one convention. The stored 7 / 4 / 12 is the slow end of the evidence (typical parties 3.5-4 up, 2-3 down), and is kept: only an approach was added.

Day trip from Highway 20 with no camp (3 timed reports). The stored 5.25 hr up and 3.25 hr down match a car-to-summit report (5.13 / 3.25), so the summit leg already starts at the car; with no approach stored the Planner added a 5.3 hr walk-in in front of it. Approach 0 makes the stored legs one convention; the stored legs are kept.

Day trip from the end of the forest road (2 agreeing day-trip reports, about 4.9 hr car to car against a stored 4.5). The stored 2.5 hr summit leg is car-to-summit (one report 2.8), so the Planner's 2.6 hr walk-in in front counted the walk twice. Approach 0; the stored legs are kept.

Day trip from Mineral Creek. The stored 4.9 hr up and 3.6 hr down are exactly one car-to-summit report, so the summit leg already starts at the car; the Planner added a 4.1 hr walk-in in front of it. Approach 0 states the convention the stored legs came from; the stored legs are kept.

Day trip from the Hozomeen Ranger Station is the usual style. The stored 7.1 hr up and 6 hr down are exactly one car-to-summit report, so the summit leg already starts at the car; the Planner added a 7.6 hr walk-in in front of it. Approach 0; the stored legs are kept.

The stored 10 hr summit leg is car-to-summit: two timed parties reached the 7,100 ft bivy in 8 and 9.25 hr and the summit 1-2.5 hr later (9-11.75 hr from the car), so the Planner's 4.9 hr walk-in in front of it counted the approach twice. Approach 0; the stored legs are kept (the stored 16 hr descent is long against 7.5-11 reported, not short, so the rule leaves it).

Empty row. Day trip from the Fourmile Creek gate (12,000 ft; 5.25 mi round trip, 2,100 ft). Five timed parties put car to summit at a median 2.25 hr and three put summit to car at 1.67 hr (3.5-4 hr moving car to car). Full set written; total is the sum of the legs.

Empty row (Capitol Peak, Knife-Edge). Published Capitol Creek trailhead to Capitol Lake 2.5-3 hr and car to car 10-14 hr; three timed parties agree on lake to summit (3.5, 3.5, 4 hr) and summit back to the car (5.5, 5.75, 6 hr). Full set 2.75 / 3.5 / 5.75 / 12.

ownerDecision.question: Store a car-to-car total ALONE on an empty row (the whole-day shape the Planner already reads for many WA rows)? The rule used so far writes an empty row only as a full set or a lone approach/descent, so these were NOT written. Several 'published' figures are guide-site summaries read as search snippets.
ownerDecision.answer: Owner, 2026-10-28: "do what you recommend based on research". Recommended and done: store a car-to-car total alone (totalHrs only, which the Planner reads as one whole day) where it clears the usual bar (a readable guidebook or club figure, 3 timed reports, or 2 agreeing within 15%, fast parties left out). 10 written, 10 held.
